history.dynasty: Guhila (later Sisodia) dynasty of Mewar; Bappa Rawal, Hamir Singh, Rana Kumbha, Rana Raimal
history.period: Original 734 AD (tradition per Ekalinga Mahatmya); present form largely 15th century (verify - some sources date the complex's beginning to 971 AD, conflict flagged)
history.summary: Eklingji is the kuldevta (ruling deity) of Mewar - the Maharanas ruled as his Dewan (minister). The original temple was traditionally built in 734 AD by Bappa Rawal, founder of the Mewar dynasty. The original temple and idol were destroyed during Delhi Sultanate invasions. Hamir Singh (14th century) installed the earliest extant idol and renovated; Rana Kumbha (15th century) rebuilt the temple and built a Vishnu temple, his 1460 inscription calling him 'the personal servant of Ekling'. Ghiyath Shah of the Malwa Sultanate devastated the temple in the late 15th century; Kumbha's son Rana Raimal (r. 1473-1509) defeated and captured him, used the ransom to fund the last major rebuilding, and installed the present murti. One source (templetimings.in) credits the final pratistha to Maharana Raimal's reign per a south-wall inscription. The walled complex holds 108 temples and shrines (corresponding to the 108 rudraksha beads). The sect history is layered: likely Pashupata originally, then Nath custody, Ramanandi control from the 16th century (per Wikipedia). Date conflict flagged: en-academic.com/tourmet.com date the complex's beginning to 971 AD, while the Ekalinga Mahatmya tradition dates the original to 734 AD. Coordinates are the geocoded 'Jai Ekling Ji, Girwa' FULL_ADDRESS match (relevance 100).

name: Eklingji Temple
town: Eklingji (village Kailashpuri, Girwa tehsil, ~22 km north of Udaipur)
town_description: Eklingji is a temple town in Udaipur district, about 22 km north of Udaipur on the Udaipur-Nathdwara route, set in a valley of the Aravalli hills. It is the foremost of the four major pilgrimage sites of Mewar and sits near Nagda, the former Mewar capital, famed for the Sas-Bahu and Adbudji temples about 1 km away. The Indrasagar lake lies near the complex.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism; originally Pashupata, later Nath, Ramanandi from 16th century - verify)
